listening1.context: You are going to hear a conversation between Salma and Yousef.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Hi Salma! You look very happy today. What is the news? Did you pass your science test?

script.speaker: Salma
script.text: Hi Yousef! No, not yet, but I have other good news. My old phone stopped working last week, so my father says I can buy a new smartphone. Could you help me choose one?

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Of course, I would love to. When are you going to the shop?

script.speaker: Salma
script.text: I wanted to go on Tuesday, but my father works late that day. So we will go on Thursday afternoon, after school.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Good. Choosing a phone can be difficult, because there are so many models in the shops. First, think about your budget. How much can you spend?

script.speaker: Salma
script.text: My father says I can spend a maximum of one hundred and fifty rials. My cousin paid two hundred for his phone, but that is too expensive for me.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: One hundred and fifty is a good budget. Now, which feature is the most important for you?

script.speaker: Salma
script.text: Well, the camera is nice, and a big screen is useful, but the battery matters most. My old phone died every afternoon, and I could not even call my mother when I needed her.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Then choose a phone with a battery that lasts the whole day. Before you go to the shop, I suggest that you read some online reviews. Customers often tell the truth about a phone.

script.speaker: Salma
script.text: That is a good idea. I usually watch adverts, but they only show the good points of a phone.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Exactly. Another thing to think about is memory. Do you take many photos or record many videos?

script.speaker: Salma
script.text: Yes, I take hundreds! My old phone only had thirty-two gigabytes, and it was always full.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Then you need at least sixty-four gigabytes. My brother has one hundred and twenty-eight, but those phones cost much more.

script.speaker: Salma
script.text: Sixty-four sounds right for me. I will also buy a strong case, because I always drop my phone. I already have a charger and headphones at home.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: That is very sensible. Please send me a message when you buy it. I would like to see it, and I can help you to set it up if you want.

script.speaker: Salma
script.text: Of course I will, and I would love some help with the setting up. Thank you so much for your help today! Let me buy you lunch next week.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Thank you, but there is no need. A fresh juice is enough for me.

script.speaker: Salma
script.text: Deal! I will bring one to school on Sunday.

items.q: When will Salma go to the shop?
What is the maximum Salma can spend on the phone?
Which feature is the most important for Salma?
What does Yousef suggest doing before going to the shop?
How much memory does Salma need at least?
What will Salma buy together with the phone?
What will Salma bring Yousef on Sunday?

listening2.context: You are going to hear a talk about nuclear power.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Good morning, everyone. Today I am going to talk about nuclear power.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Nuclear power is a way of making electricity. It does not burn coal, oil or gas. Instead, it uses a metal called uranium as fuel. Inside a nuclear power station, the atoms of uranium are split. This process releases a huge amount of heat. The heat boils water and makes steam, and the steam turns a turbine. The turbine drives a generator, and the generator produces electricity.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: One big advantage of nuclear power is that a very small amount of uranium can produce a lot of energy. A small piece of fuel, about the size of a fingertip, can give as much energy as about one tonne of coal.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Another advantage is that nuclear power stations do not release carbon dioxide while they are working. Coal and gas stations release a lot of it, and it is one of the main causes of global warming. So nuclear power can help to fight climate change.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: The history of nuclear power is quite short. The first nuclear power station that sent electricity to a public network started work in the Soviet Union in nineteen fifty-four. Today, nuclear power stations work in more than thirty countries, and together they produce about ten percent of the world's electricity.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: However, nuclear power has some problems. The biggest problem is the waste. Used fuel stays dangerous for thousands of years. Experts put it into strong containers and store it deep underground. Also, building a nuclear power station is very expensive, and it takes many years.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Many people worry about accidents. There have been two very serious accidents, at Chernobyl in nineteen eighty-six and at Fukushima in twenty eleven. But we should remember that serious accidents are very rare, and modern stations have many safety systems.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: In conclusion, nuclear power gives a lot of clean electricity, but it needs careful planning and safe storage of waste. Each country must think about the cost, the safety and the needs of its people before it decides. Thank you for listening.

short.q: What metal do nuclear power stations use as fuel?
Which gas do nuclear power stations not release while they are working?
In which year did the first nuclear power station send electricity to a public network?
Where do experts store the dangerous waste?

tf.statement: A very small amount of uranium can produce a lot of energy.
Nuclear power stations burn coal to make steam.
Nuclear power produces about ten percent of the world's electricity.
Serious accidents at nuclear power stations are common.

reading1.title: Heat Waves
passage: A heat wave is a period of unusually hot weather that lasts for several days or more. There is no single number for every country, because "hot" depends on the place. For example, a temperature that feels normal in Oman in summer could be a serious heat wave in northern Europe.

Heat waves usually happen when an area of high pressure stays over a region for a long time. The high pressure pushes warm air down towards the ground and traps it there. The sky is clear, so the sun heats the land day after day. At night, the heat cannot escape, so people and animals cannot cool down.

Scientists say that heat waves are becoming more frequent and stronger in many parts of the world. They link this to global warming, which is caused mainly by burning fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas. In fact, the last ten years included the warmest years ever recorded.

Heat waves can be dangerous for our health. Too much heat can cause headaches, dizziness and heat stroke, which is a serious emergency. Elderly people, babies and people who work outdoors are at the greatest risk. Doctors advise everyone to drink water regularly, to stay in the shade and to wear light, loose clothes.

Heat waves also affect nature and cities. Crops can die, rivers can become very low, and forest fires can start easily. Cities are often hotter than the countryside because concrete and roads absorb the heat during the day and release it slowly at night. In addition, people use air conditioners more, so the demand for electricity rises and power cuts can happen.

What can we do? Governments can plant more trees, build parks and send text messages to warn people before a heat wave arrives. Some cities paint roofs white because white surfaces reflect sunlight. As individuals, we can check on our elderly neighbours and reduce our carbon footprint, so that future heat waves will be less severe. Small actions by many people can make a big difference.

mcq.q: According to the passage, a heat wave is ________.
options: a very strong wind that lasts for days
a period of unusually hot weather

mcq.q: Why is there no single number for every country?
options: Because heat waves never last long

options: Elderly people, babies and outdoor workers

mcq.q: Why are cities often hotter than the countryside?
options: They are closer to the sea

mcq.q: What can governments do to help people?
options: Send text messages as a warning

reading2.title: The Ancient Olympic Games
passage: The Olympic Games are the biggest sports event in the world today, but their story began more than two thousand years ago in Ancient Greece.

The first recorded ancient Games took place in 776 BC in a town called Olympia, in the south of Greece. They were held in honour of Zeus, the king of the Greek gods, and they took place every four years. Many Greeks travelled for days to watch, and thousands of people camped near the sports ground because there were not enough houses for everyone.

At first, there was only one event: a short running race of about two hundred metres. Later, as the Games became more popular, the Greeks added longer races, wrestling, boxing, the long jump, and throwing the discus and the javelin. The most exciting event for the crowds was the chariot race, in which men drove carts pulled by horses.

Only free Greek men were allowed to compete, and married women were not allowed to watch. The athletes trained for months, and they had to promise to follow the rules of the Games. Judges watched every event carefully, and an athlete who cheated had to pay a fine.

The Greek cities often fought each other, but they agreed to stop fighting during the Games. This peace allowed athletes and visitors to travel safely to Olympia, even if they came from cities that were enemies in other months of the year.
The winners did not receive gold medals. Instead, each winner was given a crown of olive leaves. However, he returned home as a hero, and his city often gave him gifts, such as free meals.
The ancient Games continued for more than one thousand years. At the end of the fourth century AD, a Roman emperor called Theodosius stopped them, and for a very long time nobody held them again.

The idea did not die, however. In 1896, a Frenchman called Pierre de Coubertin organised the first modern Olympic Games in Athens, the capital of Greece. Today, athletes from more than two hundred countries take part in the Games, which are held every four years.

chart.title: Devices Used for Homework by Boys and Girls
chart.model:
The bar chart illustrates the devices that Grade 10 boys and girls use to do their homework. Overall, boys preferred the laptop, whereas girls preferred the smartphone.
Firstly, the most popular device for boys was the laptop, with 65%. This was followed by the desktop computer (50%), the smartphone (40%) and the tablet (25%). However, the least popular device for boys was the e-reader, with only 10%.
In contrast, the most popular device for girls was the smartphone, with 70%. This was followed by the laptop (55%), the tablet (40%) and the e-reader (20%). However, the least popular device for girls was the desktop computer, with only 15%.
To summarize, both boys and girls liked the laptop. However, the biggest difference was in the desktop computer, where 50% of boys used it, whereas 15% of girls did.

email.situation: Imagine you are Hamad/Hana. Your friend Khalid/Khadija sent you a book about space as a birthday gift.
email.task: Write an email to your friend Khalid/Khadija. In your email include the following:
bullets: Thank your friend and say what you think about the gift.
Say how you will use it and invite your friend to visit you.
email.model:
Dear Khalid,

Hello, how are you and your family? I hope you are very well. I am very happy to write to you. I am writing this email to thank you for the wonderful birthday gift.

First, the book about space is a perfect present. For example, it has colourful pictures of planets and stars. Moreover, I have always been interested in space, so you chose very well.

Second, I will use the book every day. Therefore, I will read one chapter before I sleep. However, I would like to share it with you, so please visit me next weekend and we can read it together.

That's all I have for now. Please write and tell me your news. I am looking forward to hearing from you soon.

Best wishes,
Hamad
